questions.question: In the PLAN strategy for writing tasks, what does the P stand for?
options: Purpose - what is the goal of the text?
Paper - which paper to write on
People - who are your friends
Practice - write the text twice
questions.explanation: PLAN = Purpose, Layout, Audience, Notes. First identify the purpose: to inform, argue, narrate or analyse.

questions.question: Why should you spend 5-10 minutes planning before writing an exam text?
options: A quick outline saves time and produces a better structured text
Planning is required by law
It impresses the examiner even if you write nothing
It replaces the need to write a conclusion
questions.explanation: A short planning phase with an outline or mind map gives your text better structure and actually saves time while writing.

questions.question: What does the A in PLAN remind you to think about?
options: Audience - who is the reader, and which register fits?
Answers - copy answers from a friend
Alphabet - check your spelling
Attitude - be positive
questions.explanation: Audience: adapt your register and style to the reader, whether it is a teacher, a fellow student or a newspaper.

questions.question: Which of these belongs on a language checklist before handing in a text?
options: Checking verb tenses, word order and prepositions
Counting how many pages your classmates wrote
Adding as many fancy words as possible without knowing their meaning
Deleting the introduction
questions.explanation: Before handing in, check grammar (tenses, word order, prepositions), vocabulary variety, spelling and punctuation.

questions.question: What is the FIRST thing to check before you deliver an exam answer?
options: That you have actually answered the task that was given
That the font looks nice
That the text is longer than everyone else's
That you used at least ten idioms
questions.explanation: The most important check: have you answered the task? A well-written text that misses the task will not score well.
